title: Climate action plan and water heater electrification
subtitle: Also road salt, winter maintenance, Cambridge truck traffic, wastewater strategy, speed cameras and an expropriation.
overview: The committee recommended that Council approve the 2025-2030 Corporate Climate Action Plan {{vote:m8}}. It also recommended a pilot to replace 84 gas water heaters with electric ones in Waterloo Region Housing units this year, with 40 more considered in the 2026 budget {{vote:m10}}. Tenants would be compensated for higher electricity bills, and Council would see pilot results before any longer program.

On roads, the committee recommended speed camera and school zone by-law changes and several traffic control changes. It backed a motion urging the province to create limited liability rules and training standards for snow and ice contractors, aiming to cut road salt use {{vote:m13}}. It also asked staff to review last winter's maintenance operations before the 2026 budget {{vote:m14}}.

Staff reported that the Cambridge truck diversion cut truck traffic by roughly 60 per cent but has not solved the problem for residents on one stretch of Ainsley Street. That report was received for information, and staff will pursue enforcement. The committee also recommended starting expropriation of part of one property on Erb Street West for road improvements.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the five-year plan to cut the Region's own greenhouse gas emissions {{vote:m8}}.

decisions.item: Electrification of Waterloo Region Housing water heaters
decisions.detail: The committee recommended a pilot swapping 84 gas water heaters for electric in affordable housing in 2025, with 40 more considered in 2026 budget deliberations and a report back on results {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended that Council approve the guiding principles for updating the Region's wastewater treatment strategy {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: School and community safety zone by-law changes
decisions.detail: The committee recommended amending the Traffic and Parking By-law school zone, speed and community safety zone schedules, effective May 26, 2025, to support the speed camera program.

The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to start expropriating a partial taking and temporary grading easement at 658 Erb Street West for road improvements and a roundabout {{vote:m11}}.

The committee recommended that the Region urge the province to develop limited liability legislation, contractor training and standard best practices, and to fund an expert advisory committee on salt {{vote:m13}}.

The committee directed the Commissioner of Transportation to review 2024/2025 winter maintenance, including ION corridor and cycling track clearing, and report before the 2026 budget process {{vote:m14}}.
The committee recommended declaring certain lands surplus and authorizing a land exchange with the City of Kitchener, at nominal cost, for the Bleams Road extension {{vote:m12}}.

debate: On road salt, delegates from an industry association and an environmental coalition said liability fears push contractors to over-salt and that insurance costs are driving contractors out of business. One councillor worried that limiting liability could weaken accountability. The mover said the motion reassigns liability to property owners for trained, accredited contractors. Another councillor noted property owners' insurance costs could rise.

On water heaters, councillors asked how tenants would be protected from higher electricity bills and how the cost estimates would hold as rates change. One councillor said Council should not commit mid-budget cycle to a ten-year program before seeing pilot data, which led to the amendment on wording for the 2026 and later steps {{vote:m9}}.

On the climate plan, councillors asked how the community would be engaged beyond Regional operations. They also asked how bus electrification costs fit with current battery limits. Staff said airport emissions are not in the modelling, and that annual progress reports and a phased carbon budget would keep Council informed.

On Cambridge truck traffic, a resident delegate described frequent trucks, noise and safety concerns on Ainsley Street. Councillors asked for more enforcement and a fresh look at a fourth river crossing. Staff preferred to consider that within the integrated mobility plan and said the main challenge is where diverted trucks go next.
